The entire territory #7 is frozen because the problem it addresses (mechanical venous trauma from rigid implant) is not established as real for a both-ends-anchored implant in a compliant vein.

territories.name: Patient-specific / adaptive eShunt
territories.v7_finding: ShuntCheck comparator attack SURVIVES. ShuntCheck (non-invasive thermal flow detector) exists for VP shunts only — 3 papers, 5 clinical trials, ALL VP shunt. eShunt is endovascular (venous sinus), NOT skin-accessible. No existing monitoring solution for eShunt. Proposed eShunt system: continuous (vs episodic), endovascular (vs skin-surface), pressure gradient (vs thermal flow). Residual unsolved problem CONFIRMED: eShunt patients have NO obstruction monitoring solution. Identifiability pre-check PASSES: obstruction has distinct temporal signature (sustained) vs posture (transient) vs cough (brief) vs drift (monotonic). #1 V25 collinearity does NOT apply — temporal patterns provide orthogonal information.

territories.what_is_genuinely_new: (1) Continuous monitoring vs ShuntCheck episodic, (2) Endovascular location vs skin-surface, (3) Pressure gradient vs thermal flow, (4) eShunt patient population unserved by any existing technology
